test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 04 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The real gross domestic product (GDP) is calculated in a way such that, the goods and services are evaluated at ______.

options.text: prices set by world trade organisation
prices set by International monetary fund
the lowest prices observed in the economy

solution:
The correct answer is __**some constant set of prices**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Real Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** is an inflation-adjusted measure that reflects the value of all goods and services produced by an economy in a given **year**.
 
• It is calculated by evaluating goods and services at **some constant set of prices**, which are prices from a predetermined **base year**.
 
• By using **constant prices**, the effect of **inflation** or **deflation** is removed, allowing for a comparison of the **actual volume** of production between different time periods.
 
• The primary purpose of calculating **Real GDP** is to track the **true growth** of the economy. If **Real GDP** increases, it signifies that the economy is producing more goods and services, rather than just selling the same amount at higher prices.
 
• In contrast, **Nominal GDP** evaluates production at **current market prices**, meaning it can increase simply because prices have risen, even if the **quantity** of output remains the same.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nominal GDP**: This refers to the **GDP** calculated at **current year prices**. It reflects both changes in **output** and changes in **prices**. While it is useful for understanding the current size of the economy, it is not a reliable indicator of **economic growth** over time.
 
• **GDP Deflator**: It is an economic metric that converts **Nominal GDP** into **Real GDP**. It is a measure of the level of prices of all new, domestically produced, final goods and services in an economy. The formula is: **(Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100**.
 
• **Base Year**: This is the benchmark year against which **economic data** is compared. In **India**, the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** currently uses **2011-2012** as the **base year** for calculating **GDP**.
 
• **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**: While **Real GDP** measures internal growth, **PPP** is used to compare the **economic productivity** and **standard of living** between countries by adjusting for the **cost of living** and **inflation rates**.
 
• **National Statistical Office (NSO)**: In **India**, the **NSO** is the nodal agency responsible for the release of **GDP** estimates. It operates under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of International Organizations**: Agencies like the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** monitor global **GDP** trends, but they do not set the prices for a country's internal **Real GDP** calculation. Each country determines its own **base year** and **constant price** metrics.
 
• **Comparison of Real vs. Nominal**: If an economy has high **inflation**, the **Nominal GDP** will be significantly higher than the **Real GDP**. If **Real GDP** is higher than **Nominal GDP**, it indicates **deflation** relative to the **base year**.
 
• **Formula for Real GDP**: It can be derived as **Real GDP = Nominal GDP / (Price Index / 100)**. This allows researchers to isolate the **quantity** factor from the **price** factor.
 
• **Use in Policy**: **Central Banks**, such as the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, use **Real GDP** data to formulate **monetary policy**, adjust **interest rates**, and manage **inflation targets**.
